answer: Separate partner confirmation deposit is the mechanism. Each identity pays a fixed coordination fee per outbound request, refunded only after two unconnected identities confirm the work; confirmations from the same operator or cluster do not count. An attacker therefore pays that fee for every fake identity and every request, and cannot recover it through self-confirmation, so the per-identity cost scales with the number of duplicates. This velvet rule turns each whisper of fake coordination into a paid act, leaving no free haven for sybil identities.
